$comment: The route table, as data. A hardcoded list means every product launch edits the core
gateway — exactly the coupling the platform exists to avoid.
`product` names the entitlement a request needs. Routes with no product are platform
surfaces every customer has: signing in, their own organization, their own profile.
Longest prefix wins, so a nested route can belong to a different service than its
parent without the shorter prefix swallowing it.
The scheduler, eventbridge and config services carry no gateway prefix on purpose:
they are consumed service-to-service (cron fan-out, the event bus, runtime config)
and are never reachable from a customer request.
The storefront pair is two entries on one upstream, and the split is deliberate (ADR-0010
§4). Longest prefix wins, so `/api/v1/storefront/public` resolves first and carries **no**
`product` key: the anonymous buyer surface is not entitlement-gated. The proxy's public
branch returns before the entitlement check anyway, so a product key there would be inert —
and an inert guard that looks like a guard is worse than none. Splitting the entry makes
that a fact in this table instead of a consequence of statement ordering in the gateway.
The public path itself is exact-matched from `STOREFRONT_PUBLIC_PATHS` in the gateway's
own `app/main.py`; a prefix here does not make anything public.
`/api/v1/auth/operator` is `blocked`: longer than the `/api/v1/auth` entry below, so it
wins the match for every operator sign-in path and is refused with 404 before any token is
even decoded. Operator sign-in belongs to admin-gateway alone (ADR-0003 §2) — the route
itself takes no principal (staff credentials travel in the request body), so an ordinary
tenant's own valid bearer token would otherwise have been enough to reach it here. Fixes
the security review's MAJOR 3.
`/api/v1/webhooks/whatsapp` is Meta's callback. It carries no bearer token — Meta signs the
body and notification verifies it — so it is declared public in the gateway's own
`app/main.py` (`WEBHOOK_PUBLIC_PATHS`, exact path, GET and POST only), and says how large a
body it may carry: Meta documents up to 3 MiB, over the 2 MiB default. The prefix and the
cap must match `infrastructure/edge/routes.prod.json`; tests/infra checks it.
The three `/api/v1/webhooks/whatsapp/deauthorize|data-deletion|data-deletion-status`
entries are Facebook Login's deauthorize and data-deletion callbacks (a different Meta
trust scheme, `signed_request` rather than `X-Hub-Signature-256` — see docs/whatsapp/
webhooks.md), also declared public in `WEBHOOK_PUBLIC_PATHS`. Their own body cap is far
smaller than the WhatsApp webhook's: a signed_request is a couple hundred bytes, never a
batch of events.
`/api/v1/payment` is payment-service's tenant surface (the organization's own Razorpay
connection and the collections reconciliation report, ADR-0024 §8) and
`/api/v1/webhooks/razorpay/collections` is a tenant's own Razorpay webhook — public in
`WEBHOOK_PUBLIC_PATHS` (POST only), authenticated by that merchant's HMAC, 256 KiB cap.
`/api/v1/webhooks/collections` is the provider-neutral path for the same handler (ADR-0033,
Cashfree merchants register it): public for POST only, same cap, provider from the account row.
